items.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: I performed with the Artie Shaw Band and Dick Johnson, another master.

ctx.x: I had an opportunity once, there used to be a jazz club in Hartford, Tobacco Valley, and they had a summer series. And at one point I became the house drummer. And Charlie Ventura came through, a great jazz saxophone player, Billy Butterfield came through, phenomenal, and I got to play with these people and learn from them. And they were of course apprehensive coming into what they would call a local area, using a local rhythm

section, but they were happy, most of the time they were happy. So I look back fondly on that. And certainly playing with some of the big bands, I performed with the Artie Shaw Band and Dick Johnson, another master. And each time I play with these people there’s something that I learn. The learning process is continuing, it’s wonderful.
We haven’t talked too much about the dancing aspect. Those engagements that you mentioned, Charlie Ventura, were they dance places or were they more listening rooms?
